# Dead Internet Theory

**Dead internet theory** (DIT) is the proposition that the majority of online activity is now generated by bots and by artificial intelligence rather than by human beings.[1] It is discussed at length in Part 8 of [[the-werewolf-game|The Werewolf Game]] series at [[badlands-media|Badlands Media]], where [[american-hypnotist|American Hypnotist]] uses it as the technological half of his concept of [[cyber-necromancy|cyber-necromancy]].[1]

## Claims and evidence cited

The article notes that Wikipedia classifies dead internet theory as a conspiracy theory, and questions how theoretical it actually is.[1] It cites a report by the cybersecurity company Barracuda stating that approximately 64% of web activity is conducted by bots and that 40% of all online activity consists of malicious bots running various forms of attack script.[1] The author concedes he is not a computer expert and can neither verify nor debunk those figures, but says they match his everyday experience of the internet.[1] Malicious bots are described as capable of running attack scripts, scraping private data and skewing the feedback of information.[1]

## Anecdotal indicators

Following the assassination attempt on [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]], the author reports seeing dozens of posts on Twitter/X by progressives and Democrats that were upvoted to extremes — frequently exceeding 100,000 likes — while their comment sections were entirely negative, which he argues cannot be organic because universally hated messages do not receive 100,000 upvotes.[1] A second indicator offered is comment sections filled with accounts repeating mainstream-media talking points almost word for word, with repetitiveness and lack of originality as the diagnostic markers.[1] The author observes that the same behaviour is present in human [[npc-non-player-character|NPCs]], leading to his claim that NPCs, demons and bots have a great deal in common.[1]

## Occult reading

Because the essay treats language as a conduit of power, it argues that the very popularity of the phrase "dead internet" carries occult significance: a *dead* internet is held to exert influence over *living* beings, forming one channel by which an engineered impression of current events is written into mass consciousness.[1]
